# Review (pass 1) — hammurabi-epilogue-4 (Col. XLIII 81 – XLIV 91)

Reviewer: adversarial pass 1. `units.json` edited in place by script (json load/modify/dump, `ensure_ascii=False`, indent 1; the untouched file round-trips byte-identically; the pre-edit copy is in the session scratchpad only). `python3 ../run3/signs.py check`: in sync (no sign added or changed; none was needed). Nothing built, published or committed; no file touched but `units.json` and this one. Notes of this review that quote Harper's dotted letters write q.

## Counts

Edits (one entry per field changed): **63** — high 14, medium 27, low 22. Distinct findings: 24 (several entries are one finding touching `l`/`i`/`n`/`say`/lemma together). Two points are open for the lead (O1, O2 below); no finding blocks the build.

High (distinct): the taḫāzim sign (AK, not ME); the god of xliv 86 is {d}EN.LÍL = Ellil, not {d}EN “Bêl” (KID missing, new lemma Bêl); “kiss of death” (nišiq = Harper's NIŠQU “bite”, stock-phrase red flag, wrong lemma).

## What I did on the plates

Method: Harper's plates 78–82 (PDF pp. 371, 373, 375, 377, 379; this part's rows are on 375, 377, 379) rendered with `page.py` at zoom 4–14 and my own crops (page.py needs `/usr/bin/python3` here; the default python3 lacks PyMuPDF); rows counted from the numerals in the margin (row 73 is the top left row of plate 80; row 17 the shaded top left row of plate 81; row 57 the top left of plate 82, row 73 the top right); Harper's List of Signs pp. 383 (nos. 1–11), 385–399 (12–108), 401 (127–138, ašakku no. 129, gal no. 133), 403 (138–148: puḫru in no. 138), 409 (177–191: lal 181, me 184); Harper's glossary text layer (PDF pp. 160–221), read for every word whose note says “I do not know” or “Harper’s sense”; Harper's transliteration page itself (PDF p. 128 = his p. 108), which is sharp (the packet's “washed-out” notes concern the other scan). No modern translation was opened or recalled; the drafter's phrases were checked against the grammar and Harper's own glosses.

**Confirmed on the plate**
- **Line division, whole part.** By script: the 117 source lines against the units' `nl` breaks (words per line): 117 = 117, no difference except XLIII 83 (mar+ri-eš-tu-um: Harper one word, the unit two, as Harper's own glossary lists mar under MARU at 43, 83 and ri-eš-tu-um under REŠTU at 43, 83 — correct). Row counts on the plate agree for the rows I counted (XLIII 80–93, 99–106, XLIV 1–3, 17–19, 35–36, 40–44, 55–56, 70–79, 86).
- **Zamama (XLIII 81).** Row 81 = star (AN), ZA (two joined verticals), then two identical box signs with a bar and ticks = GA₂ (MAL) twice: `{d}za-ma₃-ma₃` stands.
- **MURUB₄ for qablê (XLIII 93, XLIV 2).** Harper's List no. 6 (kablu) is a hatched box followed by a box with two verticals; the plate row 93 has two identical such groups after the ù sign: MURUB₄ doubled stands (the doubling is Harper's ḳablê, a plural). Glyph caveat in O2.
- **ŠU.LAGAB for puḫri (XLIV 74).** List no. 138 draws puḫru as ŠU followed by a box; row 74 has I, NA, then ŠU + box, ŠU, NU. Stands (the key LAGAB is a stand-in for the box sign, already marked TENTATIVE).
- **HAR (not HAL) for mur (XLIV 55).** The sign is the diamond with hatching (List no. 159, ḫar, mur); there is no ḫal in this part (ma-ḫa-ar uses HA + AR). Stands.
- **Doubled signs and line-initial groups.** NI.NI at XLIV 25 (two identical signs); GIŠ.TUKUL (GIŠ, TUK) is drawn alike at XLIII 87, 95 and XLIV 3, 35 (IA at 95 is the I + A ligature, so four groups for three signs); A.NUN.NA, É.BABBAR.RA, SIG₄ (a two-part sign), ZIR-šu, ma-zu ERIM-šu (rows 73–79) have the group counts the glyphs give; row 55 (two tiers: HAR ZA … AM / KAB … TAM) and row 35 (IN GIŠ TUK ŠU / KAL NIM) match.
- **XLIV 17.** The shaded stretch is five sign-widths wide, between ERIM-šu (a star-shaped sign, then ŠU) and the last sign, AM (the triangle with a lattice): the gap unit stands.
- **XLIII 106 / XLIV 1 (li-te-ir twice).** Both rows have LI, TE (two X-shaped parts), IR (the large triangle): as Harper's glossary lists them (li-te-ir, 43, 80, 106, 44, 1). Dittography on the stone; the unit's treatment stands.
- **Harper's glossary against the notes' “Harper’s sense” claims:** checked entry by entry (see the table); six were wrong or missing and are fixed.
- **q-forms.** `qar` (GAR), `qa₂` (GA), `qi₂` (KI), `iq` (IG; `ik` in li-ik-šu-da-šu, a k-root) throughout; no ḳ anywhere in `units.json` (grep after the edits). `reading` rebuilt from the glyph `tr` for all 30 units by script: no mismatch; every glyph index is covered by exactly one morph entry for every word (before and after my edits).

**Not done:** every syllabogram of all 117 lines was not matched shape by shape against the List; I counted groups and checked the recurring and the doubtful signs. Row 41 (bêltum ṣi-ir-tum) shows five groups after NIN's two parts where the glyphs give three signs; I take the extra part for the two-part TUM (List no. 90) but could not prove it. Row 36 (li-ša-ti-šu-ma): I could not tell whether a sign stands between ša and ti (see unit 15 below).

## Findings refused (with reason)

- **“lirūršuma” (#28), long ū before -šu.** The note says the vowel is long; li-ru-ur-šu-ma could equally be short lirur-šuma. Epilogue-2 says lirur for li-ru-ur. I could not settle it from the grammar; left as drafted, with the note's own hedge.
- **litēr / litēršu(ma) as “D precative of târum” (#2, #6, #7, #17).** The li- + D shape is odd, but epilogue-2/-3 fixed the form and the house rendering (conventions: “render the same way”). Not relitigated.
- **“that is never changed” (#28).** ša lā uttakkaru is a present with lā in a ša-clause; “never” is within the force of that, `l` keeps “not”. Left.
- **“cannot” in `i` of #20/#21 (“cannot soothe”, “cannot give him ease”, “cannot be removed”).** Natural English for a negative present in a description of a sickness; only `l` of #21 had to be made literal (done).
- **ašakku as “a sickness-demon” (#19 note).** The note's gloss is hedged and the word is left untranslated in `i`; Harper's glossary says “disease”, which the note now cites. Left.
- **“the stele” / `p` flags / `ln`.** Every unit has `ln` = stele line; `p` on the first line of each deity's paragraph (81, 92, 24, 40, 50, 70, 86) is a paragraph of sense, as the runbook allows.
- **“mār rēštûm … first son (?)” (#0), “pātiat kakkīya … opens my weapons (?)” (#3), “mušakšidu irnittīya” (#13), “idlūtum manhood (?)” (#23), “lišamqit”, “lišqi”, “limallišuma”, “ibni”, “likšudaššu”:** read for remembered phrasing; each is a consequence of the grammar and Harper's glosses (MARU 43,83 / REŠTU 43,83; PATU; KAŠADU III,1; EDLUTU “manhood, vigor” 44,68; MAQATU III,1; ŠAQU; MALU II,1; BANU; KAŠADU) and is marked uncertain where the note says so. Nothing in `i` matched a distinctive modern sentence I recognise beyond “kiss of death”, which I changed.
- **“a gracious guardian spirit” / lamassī (#4).** `i` “guardian spirit” is the house gloss of lamassum (glossary: “protective guardian spirit”). Left.
- **TUKUL keyed TUK, NER keyed KIŠ, URU for Harper's UNU (#13).** House keys (epilogue-1 and the sign glossary); left.
- **The `nl` / line division at XLIV 35 (dan- | nim split across Harper's pages).** The plate has both parts on one two-tier row; the unit has one line. Correct.

## Open points for the lead

- **O1 (the AK sign for taḫāzim, XLIII 93 and XLIV 2).** Rekeyed ME → AK (reading and `tr` “AK”, `val` taḫāzim) because the plate sign is no. 48, not no. 184 (me); I could not identify the Sumerogram, and I do not assert MÈ. The sign glossary's AK entry (ak, aĝ₂, aq) does not mention this use: the glosser/lead may add “taḫāzum (xliii 93, xliv 2), TENTATIVE: Harper normalizes it taḫazim; the sign is his no. 48”. If the lead is sure of a Sumerogram MÈ for the stone's sign, the key ME can be restored; the shape argument is above.
- **O2 (sign glossary).** MURUB4's Unicode stand-in (SHU2) is visibly unlike the plate's box sign (the sign note says “nearest box-sign shape”, which is wrong for the Noto glyph); LAL stands as a placeholder for the second sign of ašakku (the plate's shape is a box with bars, Harper no. 129, not LAL). Both are noted in the units; the shared sign entries were not touched (signs.py add/replace is the lead's call).
- **Glosser must know** (new lemmas, check each against the text): Ninkarrak, Nergal; aggum (Harper AGGU “anger”, adjective “angry” is the reading), apum (Harper ABU “cane, reeds”), ašakkum (Harper “disease”), binûtum (Harper “muscle, life”; “body” is our rendering), damāmum (Harper DAMAMU I,2 “to lament”), dumqum (Harper DUMKU “favor”), gurunnum (Harper “heap, pile”), idlūtum (Harper “manhood, vigor”), imittum, irratum, izuzzum-Š, išītum (Harper “confusion, revolt”), **saḫmaštum** (Harper SAḪMAŠTU “revolt”; the lemma was zaḫmaštum), kamûm (kamiš, Harper KAMÎŠ “bound”), kašūšum (Harper “power, strength”), kirbum / kirbītum (Harper KIRBU, KIRBITU “interior, middle”), malûm-D, maqātum-Š, murṣum, mūšum, **nišqum** (Harper NIŠQU “bite”; the lemma was našāqum), naḫûm-D (Harper NAḪU II,1 “to pacify, allay”), pašāḫum (Harper PAŠAḪU I,1 “to be healed, to be cured”: the stem/transitivity is uncertain), qamûm (Harper KAMU I,1 “to burn”), tamḫārum, taḫāzum, uzzatum (Harper UZZATU “fury”), šalmatum, **ḫapāšum** (Harper ḪAPAŠU I,1 “to break, crush”; the lemma was ḫepûm), šētum (Harper ŠĒTU “wall (?)”), ṣimdum (Harper SIMDU “bandage”), ṭīṭum. **Not new but broadened:** `qatûm-Š` (add lišaqtišuma, xliv 36, UNCERTAIN: Harper li-ša-[ak]-ti-šu, KATÛ III,1), `rêʾûm-pasture` (lirʾûšu, xliv 23: “lead”, Harper ARU II,1 “to carry, to rule”), `Enlil` (xliv 86, Ellil), `balûm` (ibêllû: G, Harper BALÛ I,1 “to destroy”). The lemma `Bêl` no longer occurs; drop it from any new-lemma list.

## Plate re-verification of pass 1 (plates 80–82 = PDF pp. 375, 377, 379, rendered with page.py)

- **taḫāzim, XLIII 93 / XLIV 2: AK, not ME. Confirmed.** The first sign of row 93 (a vertical wedge with a stack of small wedges and a long bar) is the same sign, shape for shape, as the first sign of row 100 (ag-gi-im); Harper's List no. 48 (ag, ak) is a lattice-and-bar sign, no. 184 (me) a plain vertical with a bar; the plate sign is not no. 184. Harper's glossary has TAḪAZU “battle, conflict” for the word and KABLU for the doubled box signs after ù: the pairing stands.
- **XLIV 86 {d}EN.LÍL. Confirmed.** Row 86: star, EN (hook-bar + box), then a ticked box; Harper's list no. 49 draws “Bêl” and “Nippur” (EN.LÍL.KI) with the same EN + box. Ellil, lemma Enlil, as epilogue-1 and -2.
- **XLIV 41 (bêltum ṣi-ir-tum), five groups against three signs.** Re-looked; I count the same groups as pass 1 (NIN in two parts, then a boxed sign with a hook, a chevron stack and a long triangle) and cannot prove the grouping either way. Left as Harper's transliteration, as in pass 1 (already the note's position; see QUESTIONS).
- **XLIV 36 (li-ša-ti-šu-ma), possible extra sign. Not resolved.** Row 36 begins with the same four groups as row 65 (li-ša-ṣi-…): a chevron stack, a ticked block, and two block-plus-diamond-cross signs, and the same shape recurs in row 65 where Harper reads ṣi; so the plate has at least one sign more between ša and the end than Harper's li-ša-ti-šu-ma gives, which is consistent with his glossary's li-ša-[ak]-ti-šu. The unit keeps Harper's `reading` and the glossary's `say` lišaqtišuma, both marked UNCERTAIN in the note; nothing is claimed beyond that. No change.
- **ašakku (XLIV 56), second sign.** The List's no. 129 is “id, it” (Á) with ašakku shown as Á + a second sign (a vertical with a box); I could not match it to a sign in our glossary. The placeholder `?` (LAL) stays. Possible identification for the lead: the usual Sumerogram for ašakku is Á.SAG; the second sign would then be SAG (Harper no. 57), but the plate shape is not clearly Harper's SAG; not changed (see QUESTIONS).
